name: Zone read (read option)
seenIn: Covered in Football 101, Lesson 21: The option and the RPO: when the QB decides after the snap
what: The zone read is a run play with two possible ball carriers. The QB, usually in the shotgun with the running back beside him, puts the ball in the back's belly and decides only after the snap whether to let go of it or pull it back and run himself.

The line blocks everyone except one defensive end on purpose. The QB watches that end: if he crashes inside to tackle the back, the QB keeps it and runs outside where the end used to be; if the end stays wide to guard the QB, the back gets the ball and runs inside with one less defender to beat.

Teams call it because it saves a blocker and makes one defender wrong on every snap. It works best with a QB who is a real running threat; the older pitch option is the same idea, with the QB pitching to a trailing back instead of handing off.

caption: Solid white: the running back's path inside. Dashed white: the QB keeping it outside. Yellow dashes: the unblocked end crashing toward the back, which is exactly when the QB should keep it.
spot: QB in the shotgun with the RB right beside him; at the snap the QB holds the ball in the back's stomach for a beat while staring at a defensive end, not downfield. One end is left completely unblocked. Watch the replay: the QB's eyes tell you who the read defender was.
beats: Aggressive defensive ends who chase the running back, and defenses that ignore a mobile QB (or are missing edge players). Log it as a Run in the drill, whether the back or the QB ends up with the ball.
